summary: Discovery POC scoping focusing on data handling for Equinex Health. transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 mins | Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Equinex Head of Data), Liam O'Connor (Equinex Security), Sara Nguyen (Equinex Product)

Summary: Quick intro, then dive into PII and retention, then workload sizing and benchmark plan, end w/ next steps.

00:00 Jared: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round-robin, we're Redwood AE Jared, Maya our solutions engineer.
00:08 Priya: thanks Jared, Priya here. our goal is to run a 4-week POC to validate redaction and retention flows plus perf.
00:15 Liam: hi, Liam on security. we need to ensure no PHI leaks, full audit logs, and ability to delete records on request.
00:22 Maya: great, we'll outline hosted vs dedicated vs private options, but sounds like you have compliance constraints. can you confirm HIPAA scope?
00:30 Priya: yes HIPAA applies, and some state laws re: data residency. most data will be US-based but we have partners in CA.
00:38 Jared: perfect. high level success criteria — 1) automated redaction meets your rules on sample prompts, 2) 95th perc latency < 400ms for typical queries in pilot, 3) deletion/retention workflows validated, and 4) audit logs capture prompt metadata without storing raw PII.
00:55 Sara: when you say "without storing raw PII" — do you mean Redwood will not persist prompts, or you can redact them at ingestion?
01:02 Maya: both approaches supported. hosted defaults to configurable retention + option to redact at ingest. Dedicated and Private give more control: prompt storage can be disabled, or we can store encrypted prompts with KMS and TTL-based deletion.
01:18 Liam: encryption at rest with customer KMS is a must. does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for private deployments?
01:24 Maya: yes for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. with Hosted we offer envelope encryption, but key control stays with Redwood unless you choose Dedicated w/ bring-your-own-key on certain plans. we'll share the details in the security pack.
01:38 Priya: what about logging? we need detailed audit trails but we do not want raw prompt text in logs. how granular are logs?
01:45 Maya: logs are token-level metrics and request metadata by default. Raw prompt storage is separate; audit logs can include hash/pseudonymized prompt IDs and a redaction flag. we can also configure access controls so only specific roles can see more detailed records.
01:59 Jared: note — there may be transcription artifacts in the recorded calls, but for the POC we can set up a separate pipeline that redacts sensitive fields before they're stored.
02:06 Liam: redaction rules — are they regex-based, ML-based, or both? we have free-text clinician notes that are messy.
02:12 Maya: we support rule-based redaction (regex, patterns) plus an optional ML redactor for higher recall on free text. ML redaction can be run offline during the ingestion pipeline or inline; offline gives you a chance to review before final storage.
02:26 Priya: what's the false positive/negative profile on the ML redactor? we can't risk removing clinical meaning.
02:31 Maya: our redactor has tunable thresholds. for POC we recommend running in "flagging" mode — it annotates suspected PII but doesn't remove it until you approve. that gives you a precision/recall matrix to decide thresholds.
02:42 Sara: OK, good. for prompt storage, we have concerns about prompt chaining and developer debugging — sometimes we need the full prompt for repro. can we have an immutable audit copy that is encrypted and TTL-limited?
02:52 Maya: yes, that's supported. we can store an encrypted archive with customer KMS, TTL of X days, and ability to trigger immediate purge on request. during POC we typically use a 30-day TTL and test purge flows.
03:03 Priya: retention settings — does Redwood support per-customer and per-endpoint retention policies? we need different windows for different datatypes.
03:09 Maya: yes, per-route retention policies are supported. you can set retention by endpoint, by label, and even by inferred data sensitivity tag.
03:18 Jared: let's talk workload sizing and benchmarks. Priya, can you share expected throughput during peak?
03:23 Priya: for the POC we expect 10 parallel clinicians, average 1 request per clinician every 30s during peak review sessions. payload sizes range but avg 1.2k tokens per request, sometimes up to 4k.
03:36 Maya: noted. for Redwood's config we need concurrency, qps, and avg sequence length. we'll propose a baseline node config and show whether Hosted burst capacity or Dedicated GPU pool is needed.
03:44 Jared: for perf success criteria earlier we said 95th perc < 400ms — given 1.2k tokens that may vary, do you want to prioritize latency or cost?
03:53 Priya: prioritize latency, but cost is a factor — we need to show per-request cost estimate in the pilot report.
03:58 Maya: for latency-first we recommend Dedicated pool with prefix caching enabled; we'll also test quantized model variant to reduce GPU memory. caching helps if you have repeated prefixes like templates.
04:10 Liam: caching — if we cache prompts with PII does that create risk? how is KV cash stored? (laughs)
04:17 Maya: ha, K-V cache — we can configure cache to store only pseudonymized representations or exclude sensitive fields. caching policy can be set per-route.
04:24 Priya: benchmarks — what's the proposed benchmark?
04:27 Maya: SE plan: run a 1k-record throughput test with 10 concurrent users mimicking your token distributions and peak concurrency; measure p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll run it on our Dedicated test cluster and also on Hosted variant to compare.
04:40 Jared: timeline — we propose kicking off week of 2026-10-19. week 1: ingest sample data and validate redaction; week 2: run perf benchmarks and iterate; week 3: validation with stakeholders and audit logs review; week 4: deliver pilot report and playbook for production rollout. does that align?
04:55 Priya: yes that aligns. can we compress to 3 weeks if all goes well?
04:59 Maya: possibly, but we recommend 4 to allow for any legal/security reviews.
05:04 Sara: about legal — procurement will want to see DPA and SOC2. Jared, can you share?
05:09 Jared: yes I'll send the SOC2 report and our DPA link: https://redwood.ai/security.pdf and the data handling whitepaper.
05:16 Liam: one more on deletion: do deletion requests cascade to backups and audit archives? we need proof of deletion for compliance.
05:23 Maya: deletion triggers TTL expiry and we can configure immediate purge across active storage, backups, and archived blobs. for Hosted we provide a deletion certificate; for Private you have direct control and logs. we'll include deletion test as part of the acceptance criteria.
05:36 Priya: success criteria recap — redaction passes review (low missed PII), latency within target under our load, deletion and retention validated, and audit logs meet format.
05:45 Jared: great. competition question — are you evaluating others?
05:48 Priya: yes, OpenAI and Anthropic for hosted, and an internal pilot on Bedrock for dedicated.
05:55 Jared: understood. we'll highlight where Redwood provides private KMS, per-route retention, and integrated redaction.
06:02 Sara: any gotchas for us to know?
06:05 Maya: watch out for very long context windows — inference cost rises with token length; we can recommend prompt truncation and prefix caching to control costs. also ensure the ML redactor is tuned to avoid removing clinical modifiers.
06:18 Priya: ok let's wrap. who will own the deletion test?
06:22 Liam: security will own verification, Dr. Rao will approve redaction rules.
06:27 Jared: next: I will send security pack and pricing by Monday 2026-10-18. Maya will run the perf test and post results by 2026-10-20. Priya will share sample PII payloads by 2026-10-19.
06:39 Priya: thanks everyone. one last note — we may need an on-prem/air-gapped option later, can you speak to that in the deep dive?
06:45 Maya: yes, Private on-prem is possible; we'll bring in the PM and infra leads for that session.
06:50 Jared: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/security.pdf, POC playbook link (will be shared), internal benchmark spreadsheet (SE to upload).

End of transcript.
